title: Midterm Elections—What Do They Mean for Markets? | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional argues long-term investors should not alter plans around US midterm elections: markets efficiently process expectations, the 2016 surprise showed even correct election calls don't yield predictable market moves (S&P 500 +1.1% the day after Trump's win), and S&P 500 monthly returns in midterm-election months since 1926 look like any other month.

insights.claim: Dimensional cautions against making short-term changes to a long-term plan to profit from or avoid changes in the political winds around the US midterms.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Base-case guidance for the November window: do not trade election outcomes as a standalone signal.

insights.claim: Market prices aggregate the expectations of millions of investors trading billions of dollars daily, which makes consistently outguessing prices very difficult, and election surprises do not always produce clear-cut outcomes for investors.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Election views are likely already priced in; edge requires information beyond the consensus.
insights.locator: it is helpful to think of markets as a powerful information-processing machine

insights.claim: After Trump's 2016 win, which many articles had predicted would sink stocks, the S&P 500 closed 1.1% higher the next day, so even a correct election call would not have guaranteed the correct market direction.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Illustrates that outcome-to-market mapping is unreliable; narrative confidence does not equal tradeable edge.
insights.locator: The 2016 presidential election serves as an example

insights.claim: S&P 500 monthly returns going back to 1926 in months when midterm elections took place did not tend to be very different from returns in any other month.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: No historical return anomaly specific to midterm-election months to trade.
